When the evening sky turned peach and purple, Coby the little trolley rolled out for his very last trip of the day.
All aboard for the sleepy ride home, Coby chimed, ringing his little golden bell.
Marlo carried a tiny green blanket, Cleo hugged a round yellow pillow, and Otis held his favorite little blue book.
Clickety-clack, clickety-clack, Coby followed the shining rails past the bakery with its golden windows.
The city lamps blinked on one by one, like little stars waking up along the sidewalks.
Marlo gave a great big yawn, but he still whispered that the lights looked like sleepy fireflies.
At the little bridge, Coby slowed down so everyone could see the moon making silver ribbons on the water.
Cleo watched the moonlit water and whispered that the river looked like it was wearing a bedtime blanket.
Around the next corner, Otis spotted little windows glowing high above the quiet street.
Those are our windows, Otis whispered, and together their homes are waiting for them.
First Marlo hopped down, wrapping his soft green blanket around his shoulders like a cozy little cape.
Next Cleo tiptoed home, holding her yellow pillow close and giving Coby a tiny sleepy wave.
Last came Otis, who whispered good night and thank you for the prettiest ride through the lights.
Coby rang his bell just once, very softly, and rolled back alone through the peaceful, sleeping city.
With his headlamp glowing low and the moon shining above, Coby closed his eyes and dreamed of tomorrow's lovely little ride.
